rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deathbed regret is compelled by despair at worldly life and the terror of what is coming, when worldly choice has ended; it is too late for repentance.
rows.anchor: لأن اليأس من الحياة الدنيا وهول المطلع هما اللذان أجبراه على أن يندم على فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second excluded case is one who persists in disbelief until death; posthumous faith cannot save such a person, as other verses also state.
rows.anchor: فإن الله لا يتوب عليه فان إيمانه وهو توبته لا ينفعه يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of helpers in 3:91 also denies intercession for those who die disbelieving.
rows.anchor: ونفي الناصرين نفي للشفاعة في حقهم كما تقدم في الكلام على الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifier “while disbelievers” leaves open forgiveness for a sinful believer after death through intercession: human repentance ends at death, but God's merciful return need not.
rows.anchor: وتقييد الجملة بقوله { وهم كفار } يدل على التوبة للعاصي المؤمن إذا مات على المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses principally describe God's acceptance or refusal of repentance toward people, while describing their repentance toward God only secondarily.
rows.anchor: من الشواهد على أن المراد بالآيتين بيان حال توبة الله سبحانه لعباده لا بيان حال توبة العبد إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative distances these people from divine nearness and honor; “prepared” can mean either preparation or a promise of punishment.
rows.anchor: اسم الإشارة يدل على بعدهم من ساحة القرب والتشريف والإعتاد الإعداد أو الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gives repentance a developed account of its reality; other religions recognize conversion from disbelief as faith without analyzing it as repentance, while Christian atonement teaching can imply repentance is useless.
rows.anchor: فإن التوبة بمعنى الإيمان عن كفر وشرك وإن كانت دائرة في سائر الأديان الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Church later went to the opposite extreme by trading in indulgences and having religious authorities forgive confessed sins.
rows.anchor: وكان أولياء الدين يغفرون ذنوب العاصين فيما اعترفوا به عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are absolutely poor before God and possess no independent power over benefit, harm, life, death, or resurrection.
rows.anchor: فهو واقع في مهبط الشقاء ومنحط البعد ومنعزل المسكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an depicts humanity as lowered into misery and distance, and needing rescue from that condition.
rows.anchor: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is return from distance and misery to God: faith turns from shirk, while good action turns from sins; nearness and happiness require both.
rows.anchor: فالتوبة بمعنى الرجوع إلى الله والانخلاع عن ألواث البعد والشقاء يتوقف عليها الاستقرار في دار الكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people are inherently needy, their return requires God's preceding enablement and assistance, described as God first turning to them so they may repent.
rows.anchor: وهو توبة الله سبحانه لعبده المتقدمة على توبة العبد إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a servant repents, God's second repentance is acceptance through forgiveness and purification from sin and distance.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي التوبة الثانية من الله سبحانه المتأخرة عن توبة العبد إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's repentance is one act of mercy, described as preceding or following only relative to the servant's turn; it can also occur without a prior servant repentance, as in intercession.
rows.anchor: وإلا فهي توبة واحدة هي رجوع الله سبحانه إلى عبده بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's will to turn toward people contrasts with the desire of those who follow their passions to lead them far astray.
rows.anchor: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nearness is relative, even impeccable prophets can repent by moving from one spiritual station to a higher one.
rows.anchor: يصدق حينئذ معنى التوبة على رجوع بعض المقربين من عباد الله الصالحين من موقفه الذي هو فيه إلى موقف أرفع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Qur'anic passages apply God's repentance broadly as forgiving and accepting the turn of servants.
rows.anchor: وهذه التوبة العامة من الله سبحانه هي التي يدل عليها إطلاق آيات كثيرة من كلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy removing sins and the servant's return from sins both count as repentance; true preaching therefore calls people to repent from sins as well as shirk.
rows.anchor: من الواجب في الدعوة الحقة أن تعتني بأمر المعاصي كما تعتني بأصل الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's repentance is unowed favor; its apparent obligation is only the certainty created by God's own promises, which He does not break.
rows.anchor: أعم من المبتدئة واللاحقة فضل منه كسائر النعم التي يتنعم بها خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not compelled to accept repentance: as sovereign, He may accept what He promised or refuse repentance in cases He states will not be forgiven.
rows.anchor: بل له الملك من غير استثناء يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One commentator argues that Pharaoh's final repentance is not explicitly rejected and that God's broad mercy makes eternal rejection implausible.
rows.anchor: ومن عجيب ما قيل في هذا الباب قول بعضهم في قوله تعالى في قصة غرق فرعون وتوبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument fails because 4:18 excludes repentance at death; such last-moment regret is insincere, prompted by seeing punishment arrive.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الندامة حينئذ ندم كاذب يسوق الإنسان إلى إظهاره مشاهدته وبال الذنب ونزول البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment-day regret and requests to return do not prove accepted repentance: the Qur'an says the sinners would return to their old conduct and are lying.
rows.anchor: وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance corresponds to social moral reform: external causes enable change, the person leaves the bad state, and the corrupt disposition is replaced by virtue.
rows.anchor: ثم زوال هيئة الفساد ووصف الرذالة المستولية على قلبه حتى يستقر فيه وصف الكمال ونور الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance changes the soul and prepares it for happiness by removing inward evils; it does not by itself cancel religious laws or rulings.
rows.anchor: وأما الأحكام الشرعية والقوانين الدينية فهي بحالها لا ترتفع عنه بتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some legal consequences are lifted when legislation itself ties them to repentance, as with offenders who repent and those who repent before capture for violent corruption.
rows.anchor: ربما ارتبط بعض الأحكام بها فارتفعت بالتوبة بحسب مصالح الجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance helps escape sin's ruin and attain success, while preserving hope; people need hope and fear in balance, and repentance revives one weakened by despair.
rows.anchor: فإن الإنسان لا يستقيم سيره الحيوي إلا بالخوف والرجاء المتعادلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance does not encourage planned sin: someone intending to sin and repent all along has never truly renounced the sin or regretted it, but has made one deceitful act.
rows.anchor: فإنها انقلاع عن المعصية ولا انقلاع في هذا الذي يأتي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Real repentance requires knowing the sin is harmful, regretting it, and following with good acts that oppose it and demonstrate a genuine turn.
rows.anchor: ولا ينفك ذلك عن الندم على وقوعها أولا والندم تأثر خاص باطني من فعل السيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is a voluntary return possible only in worldly life; it cannot occur after choice ends, and human claims require the rights-holder's consent.
rows.anchor: فلا مسرح للتوبة فيه وقد تقدم ما يتضح به ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot erase another person's property, honor, or life-right without their consent; conversion to Islam, however, erases prior sins and branch-level consequences.
rows.anchor: لأن الله سبحانه احترم الناس بحقوق جعلها لهم في أموالهم وأعراضهم ونفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who establish harmful practices or mislead others cannot fully undo their sin, because its continuing effects remain beyond their power to remove.
rows.anchor: فإن حقيقة الرجوع لا تتحقق في أمثال هذه الموارد لأن العاصي أحدث فيها حدثا له آثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance can wipe out sins and, with faith and good deeds, even turn them into good deeds, but avoiding sin is better than erasing it later.
rows.anchor: التوبة بنفسها أو بضميمة الإيمان والعمل الصالح توجب تبدل السيئات حسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sins ultimately follow satanic whispers; the purified sincere servants have a special station of servitude unlike ordinary righteous penitents.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء من الناس مختصون بمقام العبودية التشريفية اختصاصا لا يشاركهم فيه غيرهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report in al-Faqih says God accepts repentance before death by a year, month, day, or hour, and even until the soul reaches the throat.
rows.anchor: من تاب قبل موته بسنة تاب الله عليه ثم قال إن السنة لكثيرة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq explains the excluded repentance as one made when a person has witnessed the afterlife's reality; al-Tabataba'i says awareness of it is decisive, while the unaware may still repent.
rows.anchor: ذلك إذا عاين أمر الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says that when the soul reaches the throat, a knowledgeable person has no repentance, though an ignorant person still may repent.
rows.anchor: لم يكن للعالم توبة وكانت للجاهل توبة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The report from Abu Dharr says God accepts repentance until the barrier falls, which the Prophet explains as the soul leaving while the person is a polytheist.
rows.anchor: إن الله يقبل توبة عبده أو يغفر لعبده ما لم يقع الحجاب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Hasan says Iblis vowed not to leave Adam while his soul remained, and God vowed not to bar repentance during that time.
rows.anchor: وعزتي لا أحول بينه وبين التوبة ما دام الروح فيه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says no one escapes sins except by acknowledging them, and that regret itself is sufficient repentance.
rows.anchor: والله ما ينجو من الذنوب إلا من أقر بها قال وقال أبو جعفر عليه السلام كفى بالندم توبة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Sincere repentance makes God love the servant and conceal the sin: He makes the recording angels forget and commands bodily witnesses and places to hide it.
rows.anchor: إذا تاب العبد توبة نصوحا أحبه الله تعالى فستر عليه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says a believer's sins are forgiven, and God repeatedly forgives the believer who genuinely regrets, seeks forgiveness, and returns; he warns against despairing believers.
rows.anchor: كلما عاد المؤمن بالاستغفار والتوبة عاد الله تعالى عليه بالمغفرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says acceptance requires fidelity to the covenant; even a knowingly committed sin is done in ignorance because the sinner risks himself, as with Joseph's brothers.
rows.anchor: يعني كل ذنب عمله العبد وإن كان به عالما فهو جاهل حين خاطر بنفسه في معصية ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i finds the report text confused; its apparent point is that repentance must restrain a person from sin, even if only for a time, while “in ignorance” explains all sin.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالصدر أن العمل إنما يقبل إذا وفى به العبد ولم ينقضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals, like humans, display individual and social opinions about their needs that organize their movement and behavior in seeking survival.
rows.anchor: أن لها كالإنسان عقائد وآراء فردية واجتماعية تبني عليها حركاتها وسكناتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals show awareness of needs and devise organized means to obtain food, mates, and shelter, and to gain benefits or avoid harm.
rows.anchor: يأتي في مبتغيات حياته من الحركات المنظمة التي يحتال بها إلى رفع حوائج نفسه في الغذاء والسفاد والمأوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals can use intricate hunting and escape strategies; study of ants, bees, and termites reveals striking social organization, crafts, customs, and policies, and the Qur'an urges reflection on animals.
rows.anchor: ودقائق من الصنعة ولطائف من السنن والسياسات لا تكاد توجد نظائرها إلا في الأمم ذوي الحضارة والمدنية من الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering of wild beasts and many other Qur'anic passages, along with numerous reports, establish that animals and even cosmic and inanimate beings are resurrected.
rows.anchor: بل هناك آيات كثيرة جدا دالة على إعادة السماوات والأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجن والحجارة والأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal gathering entails collection and being driven toward an outcome; unlike the human case, Qur'an does not call the transformations or assembly of heavenly objects “gathering.”
rows.anchor: أن ذلك لازم الحشر بمعنى الجمع بين الأفراد وسوقهم إلى أمر بالإزعاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human resurrection brings a decisive judgment over disputes, returning good-doers their reward and wrongdoers retribution; animals also display some good and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ومرجع الجميع إلى إنعام المحسن والانتقام من الظالم بظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says that seizing people for wrongdoing would leave no creature, while God delays judgment to a set term.
rows.anchor: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shared gathering, judgment, reward, or punishment does not make animals equal to humans in intellect, will, or the degree of their accounting.
rows.anchor: مجرد الاشتراك في الأخذ والانتقام والحساب والأجر بين الإنسان وغيره لا يقضى بالمعادلة والمساواة من جميع الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ant and hoopoe display notable understanding, and the Qur'an's accounts of their speech imply extensive knowledge and varied perception.
rows.anchor: فإن الباحث النبيه إذا تدبر هذا الآيات بما يظهر منها من آثار الفهم والشعور لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether animals receive messengers or revelation, and whether a messenger belongs to the species addressed, is unknowable; Qur'an is silent and no reliable report settles it.
rows.anchor: والكلام الإلهي على ما يظهر لنا من ظواهره غير متعرض لبيان شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When benefit or harm is unclear, people deliberate to choose; when benefit is evident, they will and act without reflection, as with a hungry person assessing food.
rows.anchor: فمحصل حديث الاختيار أن الإنسان إذا لم يتميز عنده بعض الأمور التي يتصرف فيها أنها نافعة أو ضارة ميز ذلك بالتروي والتفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's temperaments and reasoning differ greatly, changing what they regard as possible or necessary; habits, laziness, and poverty often serve as excuses rather than actual compulsion.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما نعد في محاوراتنا فعلا من أفعالنا اضطراريا أو إجباريا إذا قارن أعذارا اجتماعية غير ملزمة بحسب الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's denial that he is an angel answers demands for a superhuman messenger by matching their proposals, while his message is that of a human receiving revelation.
rows.anchor: وإنما عبر عن ذلك ها هنا بنفي الملكية دو إثبات البشرية ليحاذي به ما كانوا يقترحونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context responds to demands for miraculous signs and objections to the Prophet's ordinary human life, including demands for springs, gardens, a falling sky, angels, or a gilded house.
rows.anchor: ناظرة إلى الجواب عما كانوا يقترحونه على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من سؤال الآيات المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear gathering are especially receptive; the command highlights them for extra care while the broader Qur'anic command still requires warning everyone.
rows.anchor: فالآية بضميمة سائر آيات الأمر بالإنذار العام تفيد من المعنى أن أنذر الناس عامة ولا سيما الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of a protector or intercessor besides God is absolute in response to idolaters' unrestricted claims; other verses qualify it by God's permission, which the polytheists did not claim.
rows.anchor: ولم يكونوا يقولون بذلك بالإذن والجعل فإن الولاية والشفاعة عن إذن يحتاج القول به إلى العلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning includes anyone showing fear of resurrection, whether belief, doubt, or a mere possibility, because even minimal fear can make the call effective.
rows.anchor: فإن الخوف من شيء يتحقق بمجرد احتمال وجوده وإن لم يوقن بتحققه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say the people singled out are believers who affirm resurrection and are the poor believers mentioned in the next verse.
rows.anchor: في المؤمنين القائلين بالحشر، وأنهم هم الذين عنوا في الآية التالية

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Other commentators identify them as polytheists who allowed resurrection, though al-Tabataba'i says no such group is established among the Meccan or Arab polytheists at the time.
rows.anchor: ومن قائل إنها نزلت في طائفة من المشركين الوثنيين يجوزون الحشر بعد الموت

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A further view identifies the warned people as all Muslims and scripturalists who acknowledge resurrection, since their acknowledgment makes the proof more binding.
rows.anchor: ومن قائل إن المراد بهم كل معترف بالحشر من مسلم أو كتابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes fear rather than acknowledgment, so its command applies to anyone showing fear; religious invitation rests on resurrection and accountability, and greater likelihood strengthens its effect.
rows.anchor: فالآية إنما تحرض النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على إنذار كل من شاهد في سيماه علائم الخوف من أي طائفة كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context indicates that Meccan polytheists asked the Prophet to expel poor believers; this resembles elites in Noah's community demanding the same of him.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين من قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم اقترحوا عليه أن يطرد عن نفسه الضعفاء المؤمنين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no bodily face or material direction; “face” is what something faces others with, so it can metaphorically denote the direction or aspect by which it is encountered.
rows.anchor: لكن وجه الشيء لما كان ما يستقبل به غيره كانت الجهة بمعنى الناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous works can be a face oriented toward God, while evil works face Satan; divine attributes and names are also ways creation encounters God.
rows.anchor: وبهذه العناية تصير الأعمال الصالحة وجها لله تعالى كما أن الأعمال الطالحة وجه للشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “possessor of majesty and honor” grammatically describes the face, not the Lord, in the verse about God's enduring face.
rows.anchor: فإن ظاهر الآية أن قوله { ذو الجلال والإكرام } نعت للوجه دون الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything related to divine nearness—God's names, attributes, religion, good deeds, prophets, angels, martyrs, and forgiven believers—is a face of God.
rows.anchor: وكذا كل من يحل في ساحة قربه كالأنبياء والملائكة والشهداء وكل مغفور له من المؤمنين وجه له تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These near-to-God realities endure by God's permanence; “everything perishes except His face” identifies them as remaining in His secure presence.
rows.anchor: فدل الحصر الذي في الآية على أن ذلك كله وجه لله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What worshippers seek from God is His face, including divine favor, mercy, satisfaction, and the means of nearness to Him.
rows.anchor: فكل ذلك وجهه تعالى لأن صفات فعله تعالى كالرحمة والمرضاة والفضل ونحو ذلك من وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Account” originally denotes numerical reckoning and extends to measuring deeds for recompense; because reward is God's, the reckoning is His responsibility.
rows.anchor: فالحساب على الله تعالى أي في عهدته وكفايته

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report calls those who deny divine decree and claim independent human will and power the Magians of this community.
rows.anchor: قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم " ألا إن لكل أمه مجوسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i explains the hadith as condemning those who deny God's relation to human acts and make humans independent creators, like Zoroastrian dualism.
rows.anchor: وهو أن لإرادة الله سبحانه تعلقا ما بأعمال العباد

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites reinterpret the hadith to target those who affirm decree, claiming they resemble Magians by assigning good and evil to a creator other than humans.
rows.anchor: وقد أول المعتزلة وهم النافون للقدر الرواية بأن المراد بالقدرية المثبتون للقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manuscript readings that combine “no decree” with denial of human will contradict each other, so al-Tabataba'i attributes that combination to scribal corruption.
rows.anchor: والقول بالقدر يلازم القول بنفي استقلاله بالمشيئة والقدرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says worldly gifts to a persistently sinful person may be gradual enticement, then recites the verse about opening every door to them.
rows.anchor: إذا رأيت الله يعطي العبد في الدنيا وهو مقيم على معاصيه ما يحب فإنما هو استدراج

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God grants a community moderation and chastity when willing its prosperity, but opens betrayal before suddenly seizing a corrupt community.
rows.anchor: إذا أراد بقوم بقاء أو نماء رزقهم القصد والعفاف

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: A report says God told David to fear Him always, especially when blessings accumulate, lest God overthrow and abandon him.
rows.anchor: أوحى الله إلى داود خفنى على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar of the warning to David uses a prohibitive form for “overthrow you,” while the following phrase is accusative as its consequence.
rows.anchor: قوله لا أصرعك نهي يفيد التحذير

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi says the verse came after the migration when the Companions suffered hardship and illness, with the punishment interpreted as worldly distress.
rows.anchor: قال إنها نزلت لما هاجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the report weak and rejects it because it conflicts with the widely reported Meccan, all-at-once revelation of the sura and does not fit the verse's context.
rows.anchor: الرواية على ضعفها تنافي ما استفاض أن سورة الأنعام نزلت بمكة دفعة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says to warn those afraid of returning to God with Qur'an and encourage them toward God's reward, since Qur'an intercedes for them.
rows.anchor: أنذر بالقرآن من يخافون الوصول إلى ربهم ترغبهم فيما عنده فإن القرآن شافع مشفع لهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so they might follow him.
rows.anchor: مر الملأ من قريش على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وعنده صهيب وعمار وبلال وخباب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrimah's report says Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have the Prophet remove enslaved and poor followers; Umar suggested complying, then verses about warning and grateful believers were revealed.
rows.anchor: فذكر ذلك أبو طالب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال عمر لو فعلت يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbab reports that al-Aqra' and Uyayna demanded an exclusive audience away from poor believers; Gabriel delivered the prohibition, and the Prophet thereafter stayed seated with them until he chose to rise.
rows.anchor: جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصين الفزاري فوجدا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قاعدا مع بلال وصهيب وعمار وخباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i treats these similar stories as applications of the verses, not separate revelation occasions: the sura came down all at once, and the same proposal may have recurred.
rows.anchor: إنما هي من قبيل ما نسميه تطبيقا بمعنى أنهم وجدوا مضامين بعض الآيات تقبل الانطباق على بعض القصص الواقعة
